candidates.title: First look: Union Pacific earnings
candidates.excerpt: Union Pacific reported a 16% increase in third-quarter profit Thursday as higher freight volumes, pricing gains and fuel surcharges lifted revenue, with intermodal traffic leading the railroad’s growth. The Omaha-based railroad (NYSE: UNP) earned $2.08 billion, or $3.49 per diluted share, compared with $1.79 billion, or $3.01 per share, a year earlier. Adjusted earnings of $3.53 per share exceeded the $3.47 consensus estimate compiled by Zacks Investment Research. Operating revenue increased 15% to $7.2 billion, while freight revenue excluding fuel surcharges rose 6%. Total revenue carloads grew 6% to 2.29 million. Intermodal volume increased 11% to 956,000 containers and trailers, and intermodal revenue climbed 27% to $1.52 billion. Adjusted operating income rose 7%, to approximately $1.2 billion. Despite the earnings growth, Norfolk Southern’s operating ratio, a key indicator of efficiency, worsened 2.8 percentage points, to 67.4%. The board ultimately voted unanimously to pursue steps necessary for termination. The railroad had received a $24 million federal Consolidated Rail Infrastructure and Safety Improvement grant in 2023 for line rehabilitation and bridge repairs, as well as $6.25 million in state matching funds. candidates.title: Is the Red Sea safe?
candidates.excerpt: Is the Red Sea safe? An accelerating return of container shipping to the Suez Canal, Red Sea and Bab El Mandeb, amid an escalating and widening conflict between Saudi Arabia and Yemen-based Houthis is raising industry concerns. Are crew and cargoes at risk? For almost three years, since the latest conflict in the Middle East began, container shipping lines have diverted their vessels around the Cape of Good Hope. Some tentative attempts were made to return to the far shorter Red Sea route earlier this year, but the US war on Iran stalled the return to Suez Canal transits. Since the summer, however, an accelerated return to the far shorter route has seen some 63% of pre-war capacity return to the route which bisects North and East Africa to the west and Saudi Arabia and Yemen to the east. Increased tensions in the region, particularly between Saudi Arabia and Yemen-based Houthis, are again causing anxiety amongst industry organisations, except it seems the shipping lines. candidates.title: Union Pacific CFO to retire
candidates.excerpt: Chief Financial Officer Jennifer Hamann will retire in early 2027, Union Pacific (NYSE: UNP) has announced. Hamann, who joined Union Pacific in 1992, was named CFO in January 2020. She had previously held leadership roles in a broad range of areas, including finance, human resources, marketing and sales, investor relations, and corporate audit. “For 35 years, she led with integrity and heart, guiding our finances through historic challenges, executing our strategy, mentoring future leaders and representing Union Pacific across the industry,” UP Chief Executive Jim Vena said in release. “Jennifer was tough — she never said yes unless she believed it was the right thing to do for Union Pacific. She made this railroad stronger, and her contributions will be felt for generations. I am deeply grateful for her leadership and friendship.” Hamann is the first woman to serve as the railroad’s chief financial officer.
